extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, applicants, administrators, grant staff)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/update landing page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource announcements relevant to grant applicants, awardees, and institutional administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the right models for research (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential. Choose models that are scientifically appropriate for the question being asked, balancing new approach methodologies (NAMs) with the need for human-relevant and translatable results.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects: application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH published a 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure describing key features and application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should learn the PF5 application format and be aware that applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests; follow the specified PF5 application instructions and prepare for the possibility of linked award splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions, use the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format and include the simplified required elements as specified in the new format. The announcement indicates a standardized/simplified structure that applicants must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to embed replication and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH's Gold Standard Science plan and a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative encourage a culture that values replication and reproducibility across NIH research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees are expected to consider replication and reproducibility in applications and awards; NIH has launched initiatives and a highlighted topic to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize replication/reproducibility efforts. Emphasize reliability, reproducible methods, and plans that enable replication where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring designation: 'Competitive but not discussed' (middle third)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications, recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cutoff, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that peer review triage procedures can designate the middle third as 'competitive but not discussed'—meaning applications may be scored as competitive yet not discussed at the study section. This reflects procedural changes to triage/cutoff policies and can affect whether an application receives discussion despite competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized peer review aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency; applicants and institutions should expect changes in review processes and administrative handling as peer review operations consolidate under CSR.
